sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Leon County?
sections.html:
In Leon County one office values parcels and approves exemptions, another prints bills and collects, and elected boards set the millage between them.

The collector's website lays out the order: value, then rates, then a certified roll, then mailed notices. Because the collector has no power over the roll, a corrected name or address has to come through the appraiser.

  • Appraiser: values, exemption files, parcel data, owner records.
  • Collector: notices, payments, quarterly plans, delinquency, certificates.
  • Clerk: deed recording and the stamp tax paid with it.

sections.h2: When is Leon County property tax billed, and when does it go delinquent?
sections.html:
Collection opens each November 1 for the calendar year, and the collector's site holds owners responsible for knowing what they owe before April 1. The appraiser's page reports the 2026 bills went out in November.

Once April 1 passes, a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, interest of 1.5 percent a month and collection costs under s. 197.332(1) get stacked onto the balance. A newspaper list of delinquent names must run within 45 days. The plan page adds that balances left on April 1 face a tax certificate on June 1.

The statewide discount ladder (4, 3, 2 and 1 percent, November to February) applies. Where a lender escrows the tax, the collector says the lender should request the original notice so the owner gets a duplicate.

sections.h2: Does Leon County offer an installment plan for property tax?
sections.html:
Yes, for estimated tax above $100, with the application in hand at the collector's office ahead of May 1. Enrollment then renews itself every year.

Earning the discount means paying the first quarter by June 30. A late payment through July 31 is taken at full price; missing it cancels enrollment and the whole bill falls due March 31. Meeting June 30 commits the owner to the plan all year.

  • Quarter one, June 30: 6 percent off.
  • Quarter two, September 30: 4.5 percent off.
  • Quarter three, December 31: 3 percent off, plus half of any true-up.
  • Quarter four, March 31: full price, plus the remaining true-up.

Quarters one and two track last year's notice, and changes in owner, value or exemptions reach quarters three and four. A seller closing mid-year should give the title company a list of what is paid.

sections.h2: What exemptions does the Leon County Property Appraiser list?
sections.html:
The appraiser's site sets March 1 as the yearly filing cutoff and describes homestead along with several veteran and service benefits. Homestead is the base for the other benefits listed, so owners should file for it first.

Florida stacks homestead in two layers. The first $25,000 of assessed value is shielded from every levy, school included, and a second layer protects value above $50,000 from non-school levies only. Permanent residence must exist by January 1, and renting the home or moving out ends the benefit.

The veteran and military exemptions the office describes each require homestead first:

  • A $5,000 reduction for service-connected disability of 10 percent or higher (surviving spouses may qualify).
  • A percentage discount for combat-related disability at age 65 or older, tied to the VA rating.
  • A full exemption where the disability is total and permanent.
  • A deployment exemption: Form DR-501M plus deployment orders.

Paperwork is accepted four ways, including fax. Counties and cities may add income-limited senior exemptions, so ask the appraiser which of those cover your address.

sections.h2: What caps and rules apply to Leon County assessments?
sections.html:
The appraiser's FAQ says non-homestead assessments cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, for non-school taxes. Homestead rises are limited by Save Our Homes to the smaller of 3 percent or inflation.

The state chart shows caps of 2.7 percent (2026), 2.9 percent (2025) and 3.0 percent (2024). After a sale the parcel returns to full just value the next January 1, so a buyer inheriting a long-held home's low assessment will not keep it. Mention this when pricing a listing.

Amendment 3 starts January 1, 2027, the appraiser writes, and leaves 2026 bills untouched. The office is awaiting state guidance, so watch its site for the next roll.

sections.h2: How should Leon County sellers handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Request a proration and a payoff figure for anything delinquent, and report any installments already paid. The closing agent divides the live year between the parties; late balances come out of your funds.

Document stamp tax on a Leon County deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the rate for every Florida county except Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk at the time of recording, and each party named in the document is liable however the parties split the cost.

Homestead stays behind. A buyer files on their own by the first of March, and a seller moving within Florida can carry the Save Our Homes benefit by filing Form DR-501T, with a three-year window counted from the January 1 of the year the old homestead ended.

sections.h2: How does Leon County compare on housing?
sections.html:
Leon County, home to Tallahassee, counted about 299,048 people in mid-2025, across 668 square miles, and it is a renter-heavy market compared with most of Florida.

Leon County snapshot, Census Bureau QuickFacts (2020 to 2024 unless noted)

Because owners occupy only about half the homes, a sizeable share of sellers are landlords with tenants in place. A rented home loses homestead, and lease terms shape any closing date.

faqs.q: When does Leon County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: The April 1 after the assessment year. From that date the collector tacks on a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, monthly interest and statutory collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Leon County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, when estimated tax tops $100 and the form is in before May 1. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, discounted 6, 4.5 and 3 percent for the first three.

faqs.q: By when must Leon County homestead be filed?
faqs.a: The first of March. The appraiser accepts applications by email, mail, fax or in person. Contact the office for the homestead amount.

faqs.q: Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Leon County bill?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser's message says the amendment begins January 1, 2027 and leaves 2026 bills as issued.

faqs.q: Who changes the name or address on a Leon County tax bill?
faqs.a: The appraiser. Roll changes run through that office, so contact it before bills are next mailed.
